text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.71% today, extending a sharp 8.83% decline over two weeks. The stock is reacting to a combination of geopolitical tensions disrupting global oil supply and domestic refining pressures: attacks on Saudi and Iranian infrastructure, mine strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, and escalating U.S. sanctions on Iran all create shipping risk and uncertainty. Meanwhile, U.S. refineries are running at 95.7% capacity with oil inventories at 694 million barrels—high enough that even with supply threats abroad, refiners aren't seeing the demand surge that would justify higher margins and stock prices.

The broader issue for Marathon is that geopolitical chaos abroad hasn't translated into the tight supply conditions that typically boost refiner profitability. Oil prices have held relatively flat (U.S. crude at $89.53/barrel), suggesting the market isn't pricing in a major supply shock despite the Middle East tensions and Iran-related shipping disruptions. Refiners make money on the spread between crude input costs and refined product sales—when crude prices spike without corresponding product price jumps, margins compress.
